Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Godzilla offers tiered plans with different request rate limits and features. Your plan determines how many API requests your workspace can make per minute, and what happens when you exceed that limit.

Plan tiers

Choose the plan that fits your usage. All plans include full API access to pipelines, connectors, transforms, events, and webhooks.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=plan-comparison.json|language=json|code={ "plans": [ { "name": "Starter", "requests_per_minute": 100, "monthly_price": "Free", "features": ["Up to 3 connectors", "Email support"] }, { "name": "Standard", "requests_per_minute": 1000, "monthly_price": "$99", "features": ["Unlimited connectors", "Priority support"] }, { "name": "Enterprise", "requests_per_minute": "Custom", "monthly_price": "Custom", "features": ["Custom limits", "Dedicated support", "SLA"] } ] }}}
{{ds:component/stat|value=100|label=requests / minute|description=Starter plan — suitable for testing and low-traffic integrations.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=1,000|label=requests / minute|description=Standard plan — most production workloads.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=Custom|label=requests / minute|description=Enterprise plan — contact sales for custom limits.}}

What happens when you exceed your quota

When your workspace reaches its rate limit, new API requests receive a 429 Too Many Requests response.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=rate-limit-response.json|language=json|code=HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1693430400 Retry-After: 60 { "error": { "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "Rate limit of 1000 requests per minute exceeded. Try again after 60 seconds.", "request_id": "req_a1b2c3d4" } }}}

Response headers

Every API response includes three rate limit headers:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit: Your workspace's requests-per-minute limit.
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining: How many requests you have left in the current minute.
  • X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix timestamp when the limit resets.

When a request is rejected for exceeding the limit, you'll also see a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying.

Best practices

  • Monitor your headers: Check X-RateLimit-Remaining before hitting the limit. When it drops below 10% of your quota, consider slowing your request rate.
  • Use exponential backoff: If you hit a 429, wait the duration in Retry-After, then retry. If you hit another 429, double the wait time.
  • Batch operations: Group multiple operations into a single API call when possible (e.g., create multiple transforms in one request).
  • Upgrade your plan: If you consistently hit your limit, your usage may have outgrown your current plan. Upgrade to the next tier or contact sales for a custom arrangement.

Upgrading your plan

To upgrade or change plans, visit your account settings and select a new plan under Billing. Changes take effect immediately, and you'll be prorated based on your current billing cycle.

For Enterprise plans or custom rate limits, contact our sales team.

Related

  • Rate limits & errors — detailed information on rate limit headers and error responses.
  • Authentication — how to authenticate API requests with your API key.

{{ds:component/stat|value=100|label=requests / minute|description=Starter plan — suitable for testing and low-traffic integrations.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=1,000|label=requests / minute|description=Standard plan — most production workloads.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=Custom|label=requests / minute|description=Enterprise plan — contact sales for custom limits.}}

What happens when you exceed your quota

When your workspace reaches its rate limit, new API requests receive a 429 Too Many Requests response.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=rate-limit-response.json|language=json|code=HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1693430400 Retry-After: 60 { "error": { "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "Rate limit of 1000 requests per minute exceeded. Try again after 60 seconds.", "request_id": "req_a1b2c3d4" } }}}

Response headers

Every API response includes three rate limit headers:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit: Your workspace's requests-per-minute limit.
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining: How many requests you have left in the current minute.
  • X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix timestamp when the limit resets.

When a request is rejected for exceeding the limit, you'll also see a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying.

Best practices

  • Monitor your headers: Check X-RateLimit-Remaining before hitting the limit. When it drops below 10% of your quota, consider slowing your request rate.
  • Use exponential backoff: If you hit a 429, wait the duration in Retry-After, then retry. If you hit another 429, double the wait time.
  • Batch operations: Group multiple operations into a single API call when possible (e.g., create multiple transforms in one request).
  • Upgrade your plan: If you consistently hit your limit, your usage may have outgrown your current plan. Upgrade to the next tier or contact sales for a custom arrangement.

Upgrading your plan

To upgrade or change plans, visit your account settings and select a new plan under Billing. Changes take effect immediately, and you'll be prorated based on your current billing cycle.

## Summary

I've successfully created the **"Quotas & billing"** reference page and integrated it into the Godzilla Docs site. Here's what I did:

### Changes Made:

1. **Created a new "Quotas & billing" page** (`/apis/quotas-billing`) that covers:
   - Plan tiers (Starter, Standard, Enterprise) with their request rate limits
   - What happens when quotas are exceeded (429 Too Many Requests response)
   - Rate limit response headers and best practices
   - Instructions for upgrading plans
   - Related links to Rate limits & errors and Authentication pages

2. **Updated the "Rate limits & errors" page** to include a prominent info alert pointing to the new "Quotas & billing" page, so readers encountering rate limits immediately know where to find billing and plan information.

3. **Updated the "API Reference" hub** to add a new card linking to the "Quotas & billing" page, making it discoverable alongside other API reference materials.

All pages follow the Godzilla design system with proper components (alerts, stat cards, code blocks, ToC, chips) and are internally cross-linked with CMS references that will automatically handle any future URL changes.
